verdict.rationale: PayPal documents registrable outbound webhooks: HTTPS posts to subscriber endpoints, up to 10 URLs per app, filtering by event type, retries, and signature verification. That is a direct programmatic push mechanism. However, the evidence never names order lifecycle event types (created, updated, fulfilled, canceled) or ties webhooks to agentic-commerce orders such as Store Sync or cart flows. Missing for 10: documented order-specific event types covering created/updated/fulfilled/canceled, explicit webhook coverage of agent-initiated orders, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my agent or backend can subscribe to order lifecycle events — created, updated, fulfilled, canceled — pushed programmatically

citations.quote: Webhooks are HTTPS posts from PayPal to an endpoint on your server whenever the corresponding event type occurs
Up to 10 webhook URLs may be subscribed per app
REST APIs, including orders, payments, subscriptions, invoicing, and disputes
